clue.text: Setter must finish off crossword to be accepted IMO (8, two words)

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the kept letter is received inside the word for the fruit juice

parts.note: must is unfermented grape juice

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the following word is kept

parts.note: final letter of crossword

explanation.surface: A setter is told he must polish off a crossword before it can be accepted for publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must' looks like an auxiliary verb but is the noun for unfermented grape juice; IMO is texting shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Me judice is Latin for 'with me as judge', the same personal-view qualifier as the texting abbreviation for in my opinion.

clue.text: FBI agents holding back German couple in the past

indicators.note: the agents keep their German letter at the rear instead of at the front, so the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: G-men is slang for FBI agents; its G doubles as German

explanation.surface: Federal agents detain a German pair from some earlier era.
explanation.definitionFit: Meng is an obsolete word meaning to mix or join together, so to couple things in an older usage.

clue.text: Not once backing school rule leaving permanent impression

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the old word for not is read from its end

parts.note: ne is an archaic word for not

indicators.note: the letter for rule departs, so it is dropped from the word for the school

parts.note: a grammar school
R is the abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: A one-time school regulation, applied in reverse, leaves a lasting mark on pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: NE reversed gives EN; GRAMMAR without R gives GRAMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An engramma, or engram, is the lasting trace a stimulus supposedly leaves in memory or living tissue.

clue.text: Lecture by an Indian police constable

parts.note: to jaw is to lecture or talk at length
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dressing-down delivered by an officer of the Indian police.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawan is the Hindi-derived term for a common soldier or police constable in India.

clue.text: Not seen a French governor in Algiers previously returning

parts.note: une is French for a (feminine)

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the title of the ruler is written backwards

parts.note: the dey was the governor of Algiers under Ottoman rule

explanation.surface: A French governor of old Algiers who went home, unobserved.
explanation.walkthrough: The dey was the title of the Ottoman-era ruler of Algiers, hence 'previously'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneyed is a rare adjective meaning unobserved or unwatched, never looked at by anyone.

clue.text: Trade secret in our works

indicators.note: to work material is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reworked into new order

parts.note: fodder letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A trade secret hidden in our factories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trade secret' reads as one phrase, but the definition is Trade alone and 'works' is the signal, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Commercial intercourse is an older term for dealings and exchange between merchants or nations.

clue.text: Starts to enjoy U2 historical tribute number?

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the opening letter of each of the next two words is taken

parts.note: opening letters of enjoy and U2
cain was a rent or tribute paid in kind, in old Scots law

explanation.surface: A fan starts to enjoy a U2 tribute act's song.
explanation.walkthrough: Number is read as a thing that numbs, not a song. Cain is also spelt kain: historical rent paid in produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucain is a local anaesthetic once used like cocaine, so a drug that makes tissue go numb.

clue.text: Led away from corrupt outfit

indicators.note: something taken away from a word is subtracted, so those three letters are removed

parts.note: a garbled message is a corrupt one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was steered away from a crooked organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' looks like a gang to match corrupt, but it is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing of a distinctive kind, the same thing as an outfit someone wears.

clue.text: Gulp engaging electronic autopilot

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so the swallowing word wraps round the letter

parts.note: to gorge is to gulp food greedily
E is the abbreviation for electronic

explanation.surface: A pilot swallows hard as the electronic autopilot kicks in.
explanation.walkthrough: George is old pilots' slang for the automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic pilot George, as in the phrase 'let George do it'.

clue.text: Judgement of tribunal overturned in Mediterranean

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down; in a down entry the run of letters is read backwards
in signals the letters sit within the next word, not built from separate pieces

parts.note: a run of five consecutive letters inside the word

explanation.surface: A court ruling reversed somewhere in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrêt is a French term for the decision or decree of a court or tribunal.

clue.text: Reticent individual accepts a bit of nursing after fit

parts.note: a bout of illness is a fit

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the word for individual holds the selected letter

parts.note: one individual

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of nursing

explanation.surface: A quiet person agrees to some nursing care after a seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: Boutonné is French for buttoned up, used in English of someone reserved and uncommunicative.

clue.text: Prone to wander around tip without a coat

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the word for a tip
letters that wander stray from their places, so they are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
a cue is a hint or tip-off

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to roam about looking for a tip, without bothering with a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone' looks like an adjective meaning liable, but it is just the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: En cuerpo is a Spanish phrase meaning in body only, i.e. in shirtsleeves with no cloak or jacket.

clue.text: I priced up my exotic orchid

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, suggesting the letters arrive in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper put a high price on their rare tropical orchid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cypripedium is the genus of lady's-slipper orchids, with a pouch-shaped lip.

clue.text: African ready, content in working weekends

indicators.note: the contents of something are what lies inside it, so the letters are found within the words

parts.note: a run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: An African worker is happy to put in shifts at weekends.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is slang for cash (as in 'ready money'), so 'African ready' is an African coin, not a prepared African.
explanation.definitionFit: The ngwee is a Zambian coin, a hundredth of a kwacha, so a unit of African money.

clue.text: Our navy's active beyond Cape Horn

indicators.note: the apostrophe-s attaches the navy letter to the preceding word, joining them as one set of fodder

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: active letters are lively and moving, so they are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: Our navy is busy on patrol past Cape Horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape Horn' is one place in the surface; split, Cape gives C and Horn is the definition. 'Beyond' puts the shuffled letters after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornu is the Latin word used in anatomy for a horn-shaped structure or process.

clue.text: Cherished goal once heading for Glastonbury early on?

indicators.note: on here means going on or carrying on, a loose sign that the letters are set moving into new order
a heading is what comes at the top, so only the first letter of the place is taken

parts.note: first letter of Glastonbury
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Was the Holy Grail brought to Glastonbury in the early days, as legend claims?
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Joseph of Arimathea carried the Grail to Glastonbury, a town in Somerset, which gives the surface its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Grayle is a Spenserian spelling of grail, the object of a long and earnest quest, hence a coveted aim in older English.

clue.text: Raise revenue after settlement

indicators.note: after says the income word follows the other, so the word for settlement is placed first

parts.note: a pa is a fortified Maori village or settlement
rent is income from property

explanation.surface: Increase income once a deal has been settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise revenue' reads as one phrase about money, but Raise is the definition, in the child-rearing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To parent a child is to bring it up, the same as raising a family.

clue.text: Before cutting examine cheese

indicators.note: something cutting into a word splits it open, so the short word sits inside the verb for look closely

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
taken as an obsolete or dialect sense of before

explanation.surface: Look the cheese over before slicing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before cutting' reads as one time phrase, but 'cutting' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Paneer is a fresh unsalted curd cheese used in South Asian cooking, as in saag paneer.

clue.text: Show R&B has dramatic compositions

parts.note: to prove is to show to be true
the two letters of the music genre
has contracted to 's

explanation.surface: A rhythm and blues show includes some theatrical numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb in this sense is a short play or drama built round a proverbial saying, a French salon genre.

clue.text: Alas in Scotland, top of whisky cask's perished with use

indicators.note: something perished has rotted and fallen apart, so the letters break up into a new order
the top of a down word is its first letter, so just that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of whisky
taken as written; the 's stands for is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot laments that the whisky cask has rotted from overuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cask's' is read as 'cask is', so 'perished' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Waesucks is a Scots interjection of grief or pity, equivalent to woe is me.

clue.text: Most of newspapers perhaps given pictures name mystic healer

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter, which is cut off

parts.note: newspapers are an example of the media
the pictures is the cinema
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Newspapers name a mysterious healer and print his photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pictures' is British slang for a cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine man is a tribal shaman credited with supernatural powers to cure illness.

clue.text: Eyestalk on member of order of Homoptera

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them, so these letters get a fresh arrangement

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for member
of shortened to O', as in o'clock, plus the insect order taken as written

explanation.surface: An eye on a stalk belonging to a member of the bug order Homoptera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like the zoological rank, but it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ommatophore is the movable tentacle carrying an eye, as on a snail, so a stalk bearing an eye.

clue.text: A Siemens set lacks luminance — absence of central cylinder?

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so that letter is missing

parts.note: taken as written
S is the symbol for the siemens, the unit of conductance
a TV set is a telly
L is the symbol for luminance

explanation.surface: A Siemens TV has a dim screen, with nothing in its central tube.
explanation.walkthrough: TELLY drops one L to give TELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Astely is the botanical term for having no stele, the central cylinder of vascular tissue in a stem or root.

clue.text: Headgear that is in fashion

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the verb that follows

parts.note: to twig is an old word for to make or fashion
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Headwear that happens to be in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fashion' reads as trendy, but fashion is a verb here, and twig is an old word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-wig was an eighteenth-century wig with its hair tied back at the nape with ribbon.

clue.text: Plant most uncommon cutting in France, yes?

indicators.note: cutting into a word splits it open so another piece sits inside

parts.note: oui is French for yes

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter, which is dropped

parts.note: rare means uncommon

explanation.surface: A gardener in France asks whether a plant is very rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most uncommon' looks like a superlative, but it means most of the word for uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ourari is a variant of curare, the South American vine yielding an arrow poison.

clue.text: Delicious food? Routine some say

indicators.note: what some people say is spoken, so the word for routine is matched by its pronunciation

parts.note: a manner is a habitual way of doing things

explanation.surface: Is tasty food just routine, as some people claim?
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the final R of manner is silent, making the two sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was the miraculous food from heaven in Exodus, and the word now means any delightful nourishment.

clue.text: Worn-out record I put in waste

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: something put in another thing is placed inside it, so the letter goes within the word for waste

parts.note: to use up is to consume or waste
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scratched old record that I threw in the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: An EP is an extended-play record, longer than a single but shorter than an album.
explanation.definitionFit: Épuisé is French for exhausted, used in English of someone tired out or spent.

clue.text: Japanese immigrant almost grasping university subject

parts.note: an Issei is a first-generation Japanese immigrant to the Americas
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A Japanese immigrant nearly gets hold of a university topic.
explanation.walkthrough: Issei is the term for first-generation Japanese immigrants, as against their Nisei children.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter or topic under discussion, the same as a subject of debate.

clue.text: Beetle's wing more likely to lose power …

parts.note: apter means more apt, so more likely
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking definition to wordplay. Wing looks like part of the insect but is EL, an architectural extension.

clue.text: … result putting cockchafer on back?

clue.text: A great many choices for tips in market

clue.text: Extend sides of rainbow about 67.5 degrees?

clue.text: About to remove label from hot sauce boat

clue.text: Remark about old Hebridean sheep

clue.text: Most brilliant good time hosting awards

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Hosting an awards ceremony makes for the most dazzling good time.
